B01.visual_intent: An isometric 0.2 x 0.2 x 1.8 m column on a ghost floor tile; three dimension arrows draw on the edges on their spoken cues.
B01.motion_claim: Each dimension arrow draws as its number is spoken.
B01.why: A physical object with three measurable extents is an isometric drawing; the side view is used later where the AXES are the point.

B02.visual_intent: Blender's real app icon feeds three identical columns, each tagged with the one setting changed; an arrow then carries all three to Godot's real app icon.
B02.motion_claim: Three identical columns arrive at one engine.
B02.why: Both tools are named: the real icons stand for them (SHOW-THE-THING rung 1 for a name that is not an interface), the drawing carries the 'same thing three times' claim.

B03.visual_intent: Godot's side view (Y up, Z across): a 0.2 x 1.8 column grows from the ground; the bounding-box cells X 0.2, Y 1.8, Z 0.2 land with the 1.8 ringed; the real log lines appear.
B03.motion_claim: The numbers land on the axes the voice names.
B03.why: The idea is a shape on axes: a drawing with the real numbers beats a metric card.

B04.visual_intent: Same side view: the column topples to the right onto the Z axis (rotated about its bottom-right corner), the 1.8 cell moves from Y to Z, the real log line shows (0.2, 0.2, 1.8).
B04.motion_claim: The column visibly falls over and the 1.8 changes axis.
B04.why: A side view makes 'which axis carries the 1.8' unmistakable; a real rotation of the drawn rectangle is honest in 2-D.

B05.visual_intent: Same upright column; a 2 x 2 m mesh outline draws around it; the scale cells 0.1 / 0.9 / 0.1 land; the real log lines (2.0, 2.0, 2.0) and scale (0.1, 0.9, 0.1) appear.
B05.motion_claim: A big cube is revealed behind the thin column.
B05.why: The reveal of what is under the drawn size is the claim; an outline drawing around the unchanged column shows it with no morph needed.

B06.visual_intent: The 2 m outline becomes an ink collider outline ('a collider built from it'); then a kraft box with a prohibition mark and 'no collision'.
B06.motion_claim: The inherited cube becomes a collider; the fourth failure is a box you can see but cannot hit.

B07.visual_intent: Three large icons land on their spoken cues: a ruler (facts a test can check), sliders (settings that decide them), an eye (what is left for you).
B07.motion_claim: Each icon lands as its clause is spoken.
B07.why: A set of three named things, each recognisable by a mark: the router's 2-D icons lane.
